paper_metadata.title: Power Law Amplitude Estimation for Option Pricing with NISQ Devices

summary: The paper proposes a power‑law scheduling variant of amplitude estimation for European call option pricing and evaluates it via a 3‑qubit Qiskit simulation encoding four discretized asset prices. Compared with QFT‑free amplitude estimation, the method reports about a 13.12% improvement in estimation accuracy at k = 9 while maintaining reduced circuit depth. The work relies on the standard theoretical quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation (O(1/epsilon) oracle calls) versus classical Monte Carlo (O(1/epsilon^2)).

experiments.description: Power-law amplitude estimation for pricing a European call option using a 3-qubit Qiskit simulation, compared against QFT-free AE as a baseline.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits encode four discretized future asset prices; a third qubit encodes the option payoff via controlled Ry rotations. The asset distribution is loaded into amplitudes, and the European call payoff max(0, i-K) is mapped to ancilla amplitude.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected payoff E[max(0, V-K)] for a European call option under a log-normal asset-price distribution, then recover option value from measured ancilla probability.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparison circuit with CNOT and Toffoli gates flags whether asset price i >= K; controlled rotation implements piecewise-linear payoff approximation.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under a Black-Scholes-Merton log-normal terminal asset-price distribution.

dataset_specification.description: Possible asset prices [3.981, 6.001, 8.022, 10.042] encoded on 2 qubits with probabilities 0.1%, 55.9%, 42.0%, 2.0%; strike price K=6.00; T=30/365; volatility 50%; risk-free rate 2%; spot price 7.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Log-normal distribution approximated on 2 qubits; prices truncated to an interval by three standard deviations; amplitudes loaded using Ry and CNOT gates.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated in Qiskit; compared estimated option values for k in {3,5,7,9} against analytical Black-Scholes-Merton value; power-law AE compared with QFT-free AE.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize log-normal asset-price distribution; load amplitudes with Ry/CNOT; construct payoff with controlled Ry and comparison circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bayesian likelihood / maximum likelihood estimation to infer theta_pl and recover option value from ancilla measurement probabilities.

speedup_claims.conditions: for amplitude estimation / option pricing under the stated NISQ-friendly power-law scheduling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims quadratic acceleration in the AE framework, but the reported experiment is a simulation and does not provide a direct empirical runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: at k = 9 in the European call option simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the overall accuracy of the option estimation results is improved by about 13.12%; no absolute error values are reported.
This is a complexity analysis result, not a hardware benchmark.

speedup_claims.factor: between classical and optimal quantum scalings
speedup_claims.conditions: for beta in {0.417, 0.625} and varying target error epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper describes the scaling qualitatively; exact fitted exponents are not reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(epsilon^-1) oracle calls (power-law scheduling between classical and optimal quantum scalings); circuit depth reduced relative to QFT-based AE
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(epsilon^-2) for Monte Carlo estimation; O(1) analytical Black-Scholes-Merton formula for this benchmark

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated in the paper; only asymptotic oracle complexity comparison is provided.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require large fault‑tolerant circuits implementing amplitude estimation with many Grover iterations and accurate state preparation for realistic asset distributions.
limiting_factors: Only a 3‑qubit noiseless Qiskit simulation is performed
Input distribution loading for realistic financial models scales poorly
Amplitude estimation provides only quadratic speedup over Monte Carlo
No resource estimate for logical qubits or fault‑tolerant gates
Results evaluated only on a toy discretization with 4 price states

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the method was 'simulated on Qiskit' and does not name a physical QPU.
Circuit depth is not numerically reported; only qualitative claims of shallower circuits and reduced control gates are given.
QFT-free AE is treated as a classical/algorithmic baseline within the same paper, not a separate experiment.
The paper claims theoretical quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation over Monte Carlo but does not experimentally demonstrate runtime advantage.
All results are noiseless simulations on a 3‑qubit circuit implemented in Qiskit.
